author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Concord City Manager Tom Aspell plans to retire January 31, ending more than two decades in the city’s top administrative job and just over 28 years at City Hall.

Aspell announced the decision Tuesday after returning from a six-week sabbatical, the Concord Monitor reported. He became interim city manager in 2005 and received the permanent appointment in 2006, after earlier roles in planning, economic development and as assistant city manager.

The retirement starts a significant leadership transition for New Hampshire’s capital. Concord is also dealing with a deputy city manager vacancy, leaving the City Council to decide how to structure and conduct a search while maintaining daily municipal operations.

Aspell arrived in Concord in 1998 after planning and economic-development work in Londonderry and Haverhill, Massachusetts. His January departure gives the council several months to outline a succession process. The city had not yet announced a permanent replacement or a detailed timetable for selecting one.
dek: The longtime city manager will step down January 31 after 21 years in the role and more than 28 years at City Hall.
headline: Concord city manager Tom Aspell to retire in January
